question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior?
rationale: Source inspection shows the missing gate, but the permanent policy defines a new authorization boundary and config contract that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design core gate
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.

options.title: Keep plugin-only
options.body: Leave core behavior unchanged and require operators to implement contextual approvals through before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies, accepting no built-in same-response confirmation gate.

options.title: Fold into broader policy work
options.body: Wait for related action-level deny, response-gate, and HITL interrupt designs to settle into one authorization model before adding a new config surface.

recommendation.title: Design core gate
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available owner signal because prior issue review already routed the choice to core product/security design rather than a narrow code owner.
